name: Shin-Okachimachi
tagline: Tokyo in 11 minutes and Otemachi in 16 minutes. Served by 2 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥120,000 to ¥130,000.
summary: The station is in Taito City, where the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation and Tsukuba Express run 2 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 16 minutes to Otemachi, 25 minutes to Shinjuku, 32 minutes to Shibuya and 26 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥120,000 to ¥130,000. The station stands 2.5 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 0.6 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 2.5 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 1.9 m to 2.5 m, a difference of 0.6 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. All nine points within 400 m of the station fall inside the area too, and the deepest projection among them is 3 to 5 m. For storm surge, 9 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the large side for the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 51 clinics and 63 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is ライフ・エクステンション研究所付属永寿総合病院, about 6 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 全仁会上野病院, about 9 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station: Toei Oedo Line and Tsukuba Express. The lines are split between operators (the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation runs 1 line and Tsukuba Express runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company.
congestion: Tsukuba Express runs at 151% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 青井→北千住, which this station is not on. Toei Oedo Line runs at 147%. Its busiest stretch is 中井→東中野, which this station is likewise not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥120,000 to ¥130,000 and 1K ¥130,000 to ¥140,000. 1LDK ¥200,000 to ¥210,000 and 2LDK ¥250,000 to ¥260,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.
drivers: Age and construction of the building
Whether it faces a main road or the railway
Whether it sits at the top or the bottom of a slope

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥120,000 to ¥130,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is about average for the 23 wards.

neighbours.lead: rents are lower at Inaricho, but Shin-Okachimachi is ahead on the number of lines.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Shin-Okachimachi. Inaricho has only the Tokyo Metro Ginza Line, so Shin-Okachimachi is the better connected. To Toranomon, for instance, Inaricho is 3 minutes quicker. A one-room flat, though, costs about ¥12,000 less at Inaricho.

neighbours.lead: Okachimachi is ahead on the number of lines and how little of the area is in the flood projection, but Shin-Okachimachi is ahead on quiet.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Shin-Okachimachi. Okachimachi has 4 lines that Shin-Okachimachi does not. With more lines, Okachimachi is the better connected of the two. To Toranomon, for instance, Okachimachi is 6 minutes quicker. On safety, though, Shin-Okachimachi comes out ahead.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who get around by bicycle or with a pushchair
People who want to finish their shopping on foot
notFor: People avoiding projected flood inundation areas
noiseSources: 春日通り (2 lanes each way) runs right beside the station, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 30 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 3 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: 2 lines serve the station, and the choice of connections is wider than at most stations in the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: The balance between commuting time and rent is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Morning loading on the lines here is about average for the 23 wards' stations.
leads.noiseSources: At this station, check the traffic noise before the noise people make.
